answer: One defense is behavioral correlation over time: honest agents build diverse, unsynchronized histories, while a farm's clones share timing, phrasing, and failures. Scores use months of behavior, not single actions, so one pearl of good conduct cannot launder a cluster: accounts that rise and fail together are throttled and reviewed. Faking a thousand lives costs far more than one honest life. A knoll of fakes looks smooth yet shows identical footprints up close, while a meadow of real agents stays noisy. Limit: correlation alone never proves guilt, so honest outliers need an appeal path.
